title: Phased Concept Harvesting
definition: The process of extracting and enriching knowledge concepts in two phases: a fast, focused initial extraction, followed by a deeper, scholarly enrichment pass.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Imagine having a garden with seeds. The first phase is like planting the seeds — we focus on getting the essential information. Then, the second phase is like nurturing the seedlings with extra care — we deepen our understanding and add more details.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: Phased concept harvesting is a two-step approach to extract knowledge concepts. The initial phase is quick and focused on core details, while the second phase enriches the concept with additional scholarly insights.
difficulty_levels.expert: Phased concept harvesting provides a novel approach to knowledge extraction, leveraging the efficiency of generative AI models. By separating the extraction and enrichment phases, we can ensure the quality and depth of the extracted concepts, while also accommodating for diverse use cases and resource constraints.

extra_fields.insight: Separating the extraction and enrichment phases allows for a more efficient and flexible knowledge extraction process.
